description: Rate application and division — the two operations that are permitted to round, and therefore the two that cannot be called without a policy (ADR-0002 §2.2). The shapes here are the ones a determination actually performs: a rate on a net amount, an inclusive extraction, a per-unit factor, a second-step tax on a tax.

provenance.oracle: General Decimal Arithmetic Specification — multiply, divide, quantize — applied to the calculation shapes named in Build Plan §W2 lane H
provenance.contentVersion: n/a — engine vectors. Rates here are illustrative magnitudes, not authority-sourced rates; a rate that claims legal force arrives in a signed content bundle with its own instrument reference.

cases.oracle: Elementary arithmetic: the product 20.0000 is exact, and quantizing it to scale 2 discards only zeros. The rounding step is still named, because a policy that is unnecessary for this input is necessary for the next one.
19.99 x 0.0875 = 1.749125 exactly; half-up at scale 2 gives 1.75. The exact product is carried at full precision and rounded once, per ADR-0002 §2.5.
12.00 x 0.06375 = 0.7650000 exactly, which is a tie at scale 2; half-up resolves away from zero.

The same exact product, 0.7650000, under half-even. One cent of difference on one line from nothing but the mode is the reason ADR-0002 §2.3 sources the mode from content rather than from a Go constant.
-1.749125 under half-up away from zero. A credit note must reverse the invoice it corrects to the cent; an asymmetric rounding here would leave residue on every reversal.
1080 x 0.10 = 108.000 exactly; JPY materialises at scale 0 (ISO 4217 exponent 0).

2500 x 0.0416667 = 104.1667500 exactly, then half-up at scale 2. A PPU factor carries precision far below the currency minor unit, which is the argument in ADR-0002 §4.2 against holding fiscal values as scaled integers.

0.0875 exactly, then half-up at scale 2. The base is the rounded output of rate-on-net-requires-rounding: this is the second step of a tax-on-tax, and the ordering that decides whether it is the rounded or the unrounded base belongs to DET-001 (ADR-0005 §7.1), not to the engine.
A tax-inclusive gross of 120.00 at 20% has a net of exactly 100. The quotient is exact and the policy still has to be named — division has no default in this package by construction.
100/3 = 33.3333... ; half-up at scale 2 gives 33.33. Note that three such lines sum to 99.99 and not to 100.00 — distributing a total is allocation (ADR-0002 §2.6), not three divisions.
The same quotient at the finer scale an intermediate tax component may carry. Authority instruments specify scale independently of mode, which is why the two are separate fields (ADR-0002 §3.3).
1/7 = 0.142857142857... ; the discarded digits begin with 1, so no mode changes the answer. A non-terminating quotient is exactly why division carries a policy while addition does not.
10/3 = 3.3333... ; round-up moves away from zero whenever anything is discarded, so it gives 3.34 where half-up gives 3.33.
